- When sentiment is consistently negative (avg < -0.3) over recent days, model tends to overcorrect upward — reduce forecast peak by 5–10%.
- After a sharp price spike (forecast > 70), model often overshoots and fails to correct — cap forecast at +5% above true peak or adjust downward by 2–3 points if sentiment turns negative.
- If sentiment is neutral or slightly positive (avg > -0.2), model tends to overestimate mean — apply 3–5% downward bias to 30d forecast mean.
- When sentiment is strongly negative and price is near 65–68, model often underestimates downward trend — add 2–4% upward bias to forecast to account for mean reversion.
- Forecast horizon 30d is prone to lagging sentiment shifts — if sentiment turns positive after 10 days, adjust forecast downward by 1–2% per day until sentiment stabilizes.
- If sentiment is volatile (±0.3 or more) in last 5 days, reduce forecast volatility by 20–30% to avoid overfitting to noise.
